questions.question: If an air compressor has a belt, the belt should be checked regularly. It should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Properly tightened.
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor drive belt before each trip. Make sure the belt is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: Keeping cargo low can:
questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent a rollover.
questions.explanation: Vehicles can roll over if turned too quickly. Keep the center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible. This helps prevent rollovers.

questions.question: When driving down a long hill, you should brake by:

options.text: Using mostly brakes and sometimes downshifting.
Downshifting first, then using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting first, then using the brakes.
questions.explanation: On a long downhill slope, shift to a lower gear first. Then use the brakes. Using only brakes can cause them to overheat and fail. A lower gear uses engine power to help control your speed.

questions.question: To avoid hitting a hazard on the road:

options.text: You should always try to stop.
Swerving may be safer than stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: Sometimes swerving away from a hazard is safer than trying to stop. You can usually turn away from something faster than you can stop completely.

questions.question: A skid caused by pressing the accelerator too hard can usually be fixed by:

options.text: Removing your foot from the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Removing your foot from the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Release the accelerator to fix a skid caused by over-acceleration. This type of skid happens most often on snow or ice.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain why you are checking each item.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain why you are checking each item.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will inspect your vehicle completely. You must explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Continue driving to finish your trip.
Drive faster to get to your destination sooner.
Safely pull off the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely pull off the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Stop and rest if you feel drowsy while driving. Tired drivers cause many serious and fatal accidents.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.
Estimate the weight of cargo on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will inspect your vehicle completely. You must explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: During an inspection, slack adjusters on S-cam brakes should not move more than:
questions.correctAnswerText: One inch.
questions.explanation: Park on level ground and check each slack adjuster. Pull them gently. They should not move more than about one inch. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment.

questions.question: A trailer that is not at the right height:
questions.correctAnswerText: Will not couple correctly.
questions.explanation: Check the trailer height before coupling. If it is too low, the trailer nose may be damaged. If it is too high, it may not couple correctly.

questions.question: When checking power steering hoses during a pre-trip inspection, what should you look for?

options.text: Extra hose pieces available for repairs

questions.correctAnswerText: Leaks
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check the power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look especially at the hoses for any leaks.

questions.question: What could a cardboard box on the roadway do?

options.text: Be expected to be on the roadway
Contain a heavy object that could damage vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Contain a heavy object that could damage vehicles
questions.explanation: Any object on the road can be dangerous. Even a cardboard box might contain something hard or heavy that could damage your vehicle.

questions.question: How does watching the road ahead help you?

options.text: It is more dangerous than only watching your mirrors
It does not help you drive more safely
It can help you avoid sudden lane changes

questions.correctAnswerText: It can help you avoid sudden lane changes
questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous. By looking ahead at the road, you can spot obstacles early and avoid needing to make sudden lane changes.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early, well before a turn or lane change
Signal continuously until the turn is completed
Don't over-signal. If no one is near you, there is no need to signal

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't over-signal. If no one is near you, there is no need to signal
questions.explanation: Always signal early, signal continuously throughout your turn or lane change, and cancel the signal after you complete your move. Always use your signals, even if no one appears to be nearby.

questions.question: When coming to a stop, how should you apply the brake pedal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Push down gradually
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down gradually when stopping. Gradual braking helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When are people usually the least alert?
questions.correctAnswerText: Late at night
questions.explanation: Most drivers are least alert at night, especially after midnight. Fatigue-related crashes happen more often at night than at any other time.

questions.question: When should you slow down for a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before entering the curve
questions.explanation: Always slow to a safe speed before entering a curve. Slowing while inside the curve could cause a skid.

questions.question: How should you park?

options.text: Share a parking lot with automobiles
In a way that lets you pull forward when leaving
Ask drivers of smaller vehicles to move

questions.correctAnswerText: In a way that lets you pull forward when leaving
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous and should be avoided. Choose a parking space that allows you to pull forward when you leave. Avoid parking near smaller vehicles to reduce maneuvering problems.

questions.question: What should happen before air pressure in an air brake tank drops below 55 psi?

options.text: The warning light should turn on
The vehicle will be unable to shift out of gear

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light should turn on
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light must turn on before the air pressure drops below 55 psi. If the warning light does not work during an inspection, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: When should the trailer hand valve be used?

options.text: To check the connection between the trailer and tractor

questions.correctAnswerText: To test the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only when testing the brakes. Using it while driving could cause a skid.
